messages:
maria: heads-up — we're getting a surge of 502/504s on hosted inference routes starting ~16:10 UTC. Several paying customers (high-traffic) reported timeouts. I see a lot of prefix-cache errors in the frontend logs. Escalating.

support-engineer: seen the same from support queue. Customer reported: requests to /v1/generate returning 502 with body {"error":"upstream timeout"}. Provided them a short workaround (retry x2) but they want root cause.

ryan: I'm pulling logs. Initial look — redis/memcached prefix cache is throwing connection/timeouts and causing requests to block at cache layer, which cascades to 502s. Attaching relevant snippets.

ryan: ```
$ curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}' -v
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< {"error":"upstream timeout","code":502}
```

ryan: frontend logs: ```
[2026-03-15T16:21:58Z] inference-frontend ERROR prefix-cache: redis timeout=1500ms host=10.0.5.12:6379 err="read tcp 10.0.2.7:41234->10.0.5.12:6379: i/o timeout"
[2026-03-15T16:22:00Z] inference-frontend ERROR prefix-cache: connection refused host=10.0.5.12:6379
[2026-03-15T16:22:01Z] router WARN request handler blocked waiting on cache for 1800ms
[2026-03-15T16:22:02Z] router ERROR upstream gateway timeout: 504
```

sam: interesting — cache metrics show eviction and CPU spikes on the redis primary around 16:05. There's also increased traffic pattern with lots of long prefix keys (KV sizes ~2-4MB) from a warmup job. Might be memory thrashing + slow commands.

eng-infra: adding context — earlier today a background warmup ran that prefills prefix cache with large entries. TTL was set to 0 for that job, so keys never expired; combined with a recent model rollout that increased request fanout, memory pressure caused redis to start blocking and rejecting clients.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED INC-20260315-42 severity:sev2 channel: #incidents; paging oncall.

maria: mitigation plan? We need immediate customer relief and a root cause fix.

ryan: quick mitigation applied: disabled prefix caching at the edge for hosted-1 via config flip (routes: hosted/* -> caching.prefix.enabled=false) and enabled fail-open so cache failures don't block requests. Rolling patch applied to frontend deployment in eu-west-1.

ryan: commands run: ```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap inference-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"caching.prefix.enabled":"false","caching.fail_open":"true"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-frontend -n inference
```

sam: restarted redis primary and flushed the prefilling job keys (pattern warmup:*). Also increased maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru and set sensible TTLs for warmup entries (3600s). Restarted replicas to clear stuck clients. Metrics are trending back to normal.

sam: redis cli log snippet: ```
10.0.5.12:6379> INFO memory
used_memory_human:8.1G
maxmemory:8G
maxmemory_policy:noeviction  <-- BAD
10.0.5.12:6379> CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
OK
```

support-engineer: customer update drafted and sent — included explanation of cache issue, mitigation (cache disabled for now), ETA for full recovery, and apology. Case #SUP-12345.

maria: good. For post-incident: we need to (1) prevent warmup job from creating huge keys (limit key size), (2) add graceful degrade path where cache timeouts are non-blocking by default, (3) alert on redis evictions and CPU > 80% within 5m.

eng-infra: will put a follow-up PR to add circuit-breaker around prefix cache client and a config to cap KV size. Also will add a runbook step to disable prefill if eviction rate > 0.5% in the next deployment.

ryan: reproduction steps for devs/QA: ```
# triggers the behavior: heavy concurrent requests with large prefixes
hey -n 10000 -c 100 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"warm: <large-payload>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# watch for cache errors in frontend logs and redis INFO stats (evicted_keys > 0)
```

maria: marking this thread for postmortem. Support ticket will remain open until we re-enable caching and verify stability. Thanks everyone for quick action. :thumbsup:

support-engineer: closing loop with customer after they verified success on retries and re-routed traffic. Waiting 2h stable window before re-enable.

sam: note for postmortem — possible follow-up: consider backing cache with a bounded LRU memcached cluster for large-value prefixes to avoid single-node OOMs.

maria: agreed. I'll schedule a 30m post-incident review tomorrow and assign owners for actions.
